On behalf of the Interstellar Coalition and the <0> Ranger Center in particular, I would like to thank all the true patriots enrolling into the ranger force in this hour of hardship! We all remember that 200 years ago it was the rangers who put an end to the Klissan War that threatened the very existence of all five Coalition civilizations. That war was a lesson to us all, strengthening the unity of the Coalition. Thanks to this war, whatever misunderstandings arose in the last two centuries were resolved swiftly and peacefully. This long-standing peace was broken six years ago when unidentified aggressors attacked a science expedition from Earth in a remote star system. According to their last message, the enemy resembled the klissan. However, the klissan always waged combat in space, whereas this attack took place planetside...
Thus the Coalition met a new enemy -- one that looks like a mix between the klissan and war machines of alien design. The machines self-reproduce at a rapid pace, taking over one system after another, fighting with equal skill on planets, in open space and in hyperspace. The earthlings from the first encounter had named them dominators. Alas, despite the heroism of our military, the attempt to crush the enemy in one fell swoop at the Battle of Gralgar proved disastrous. As we suffered tremendous losses, the dominators were able to withdraw their brain center -- Blazer -- from the main strike. At present they are continuing to reproduce on unknown bases in remote space.

Due to unscrupulous merchants doing business with the pirates and other such opportunists, we can't even keep full control of our front lines. Our brilliant strategists are hard at work concocting plans how to sic the pirates and the dominators against one another, but, sadly, nothing has worked thus far. Maybe you'll have some fresh ideas? He appears to be based somewhere very remote, and we only ever meet the front lines of his army. The information we've managed to extract from captured terronoids suggests he may be based on the surface of a planet somewhere. If only we knew what he was up to... MS_SB2.4: And how did the Coalition find out?
MS_SB2.5: Congratulations, <Player>, your services have merited a higher level of clearance. Now you can learn about the origins of the dominators. Actually, we've been privy to this information from the start, but it was classified so as to not "undermine the unity of the Coalition." Though I'm getting pretty tired of these politicians and servicemen and their secrets... In essence, they're the ones to blame for all this to begin with. The fact is that the Klissan War wasn't the first war the Galaxy has seen. Conflicts and scattered warfare between the five races were quite the norm even before the klissan appeared. Those early wars gave rise to a new weapon -- modular self-reproducing and self-improving robots. The immediate consequence was a sharp increase in casualties on all sides. And then, on one particular planet, the robots' autonomous reproducing and upgrading process got out of control. Though we managed to destroy the renegades then, the scare was sufficient to get the races to start negotiating and ultimately reach an agreement, banning any further developments of this technology and stipulating the destruction of all existing robots, along with their technical documentation. But the maloqs, the last race to develop the technology, seeing as their race was and is the most backward, didn't feel like losing it right away. And so they hid their robots on a planet in the middle of nowhere, which nobody else knew about. When the klissan appeared, as ill luck would have it, this planet ended up being one of their first targets. Though the klissan weren't entirely without casualties in the ensuing battle, victory was predictably theirs. Before they retreated, the maloqs plastered the planet with all of their firepower to keep their robots from falling into enemy hands. Everything on the surface was razed to the ground, the planet's factories reduced to ashes. If nothing else, maloqs are masters of destruction...
MS_SB2.6: After the end of the war, the maloqs deployed a scouting ship to the planet. The ship didn't land on the planet's surface due to blazing radiation levels, merely observing the planet from orbit. Their detectors didn't pick up any activity, reassuring the maloqs that everything was all right. Alas... Some of the klissan and robot micromodules ended up surviving the attack. Being capable of autonomous repair and reproduction, heaps of wreckage and debris gave rise to a new form of cybernetic life. At the same time, the original programs and mechanisms were so corrupted by the destruction and radiation that present-day dominators are immune to commands from their former masters, whether us or Makhpella. If only we could contact their leaders and understand their goals... Somehow I am certain this isn't just a war for the sake of war.
MS_SB2.7:
When the maloqs realized where this new enemy of the Coalition came from, they fessed up to everything -- at least that's the official version. In reality, rumor has it their secret was wrung out of them by the peleng intelligence... If that's true, it was one of those rare times in history when the Dzuhallag did something that benefited us all. Whatever the cause, the maloqs gave up the coordinates of that planet. And, you guessed it, the planet was Gralgar... What followed was the most terrible battle of this war to date, in which the Coalition lost two thirds of its united fleet. And still the losses were deemed justified, for the planet was destroyed. The dominators vanished from our space... only to reappear several months later with renewed strength. Evidently, their brain centers had left Gralgar before the battle even started.
And that, essentially, is the gist of it. This information remains classified to this very day. Know that you cannot disclose it to anyone.
